name: ChordPro
intro: ChordPro keeps the facts in {directives} and the chords inline, in square brackets before the word they sit on. The title and key are read as facts, so no title needs adding.

name: Genius.com
input_format: URL of a Genius.com lyrics page
intro: The lyrics of an old song that is out of copyright, read from its Genius.com page. The page adds its own text above the lyrics (the first two lines of the page text below), which is set aside; the title and credits come from the page. The last line holds a look-alike letter (a Cyrillic e in Because) which Genius is thought to use to mark its text; it is kept exactly as found.

name: Ultimate Guitar
input_format: URL of an Ultimate Guitar chords page

facts.title: When the Saints Go Marching In

intro: A traditional song, which is out of copyright, read from its Ultimate Guitar chords page. This version has chords above the words and no section headers, so the skill finds no sections. The title, the tempo (145 bpm) and the artist (listed on the page as Misc Traditional) come from the page, not from the chord text.

name: Bracket format
input_format: Bracket format: text with [Verse 1] style headers
intro: Each section starts with a header in square brackets. A header can also name a performer, as in [Verse 1: Name].

name: Unbracketed format
input_format: Unbracketed format: plain text with section labels, no brackets
intro: The labels are written plainly, as people often type them (Verse 1, Chorus, V1, CHORUS). The skill reads them as section headers.

name: Plain text
intro: Text as it is pasted: a title line, then stanzas with no section labels. The skill cannot tell where a verse or chorus starts, so it finds no sections; the stanzas are lyric lines. Claude would ask which part is which.

name: Chords above words
intro: Each chord line sits above the lyric line it belongs to. Each chord is attached to the word it sits over, by column.

name: Word documents
intro: Only the text of the paragraphs is used: comments, deleted text and formatting are ignored. The input below is the text of the paragraphs.
